messages.content: I can leave earlier Thursday now, but the morning meeting is still fixed. Can we improve the Chicago arrival margin without making the airport timing unrealistic?
Yes. What time does the meeting end, and where will you be when it finishes? I’ll compare the earlier nonstop with the 12:55 p.m. Midway flight already on the shortlist.
It should end at 9:00 a.m. in downtown Denver. I could leave for the airport by 9:10.

That makes the 11:35 a.m. Southwest nonstop workable. It is currently scheduled to reach Midway at 2:55 p.m., giving you three hours and thirty-five minutes before the 6:30 briefing. Leaving downtown at 9:10 should put you at DEN around 9:50, about one hour and forty-five minutes before departure. The 12:55 flight remains less comfortable on the Chicago end because it arrives at 4:15.
Use the 11:35 outbound, then. What are the realistic Sunday returns if the final session ends at 2:30?

The useful nonstop choices are a 4:45 p.m. departure from Midway, the 6:35 p.m. Midway flight from the earlier plan, and a 7:20 p.m. option from O’Hare. The 4:45 leaves only two hours and fifteen minutes from session end to takeoff, so it is vulnerable to a late finish and transfer delays. The 6:35 provides four hours and five minutes. The O’Hare option adds time but requires a longer transfer and gets you to Denver later.
The 6:35 sounds like the sensible one. Does changing the outbound affect the fare much?

The current round-trip listing for the 11:35 outbound and 6:35 return is about $382 on the midlevel fare, roughly $32 more than the earlier combination. The lowest fare is about $346, but its change and credit terms are less useful for an office booking.
Spell out the difference. Our travel coordinator will need to know what is refundable and what happens if the program changes.

Neither quoted fare is refundable to the original payment method. On the lower fare, cancellation produces a flight credit in the traveler’s name, and changes require paying any fare difference. The midlevel fare also returns value as a flight credit, but adds same-day confirmed change and standby benefits when available. A fully refundable fare is currently around $548 round trip.
Would the midlevel credit go back to the university card?

No. A nonrefundable ticket generally creates a flight credit rather than a card refund. Because office portals can impose their own handling rules, the coordinator should confirm whether the credit is retained for your future university travel and how it is tracked. Only the refundable fare should return funds to the original form of payment after cancellation.
Then keep the midlevel fare as the working choice. I don’t need the refundable one for this trip. Are there any separate-ticket issues here?
No. The selected outbound and return are shown on one Southwest round-trip itinerary, so there is no split-ticket exposure. The hotel remains separate, as expected.
Give me the booking-ready version, but don’t purchase anything.

Working flight plan: Southwest nonstop from Denver at 11:35 a.m. Thursday, March 27, arriving Midway at 2:55 p.m.; Southwest nonstop from Midway at 6:35 p.m. Sunday, March 30, arriving Denver around 8:15 p.m. The current midlevel round-trip fare is about $382 and is nonrefundable: cancellation should yield a flight credit, changes may require a fare difference, and same-day change or standby benefits are included subject to availability. This replaces the 12:55 p.m. outbound and improves the briefing margin to three hours and thirty-five minutes. Before the coordinator books, verify the live schedule and fare, nonstop status, exact fare rules, baggage terms, credit ownership under the university portal, and the 24-hour cancellation provision. The Central Loop Hotel plan remains unchanged and is not part of this flight purchase.
